gitCommit.subject: deps: drizzle 0.45, drop legacy-peer-deps, squash drizzle/ to one baseline (#328)
gitCommit.body:
deps: drizzle 0.45, drop legacy-peer-deps, squash drizzle/ to one baseline (#328)

* docs(spec): dependency hygiene design (purses-mebk)

Disposable data retires the replay landmine, so squash drizzle/ to one
generated baseline instead of translating 17 v5 snapshots. Reset is a
committed fail-closed script, not a hand-run operation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01K8sHMdAX2XpyuCacTHnDYv

* docs(spec): fold adversarial review into dependency-hygiene design

Three lenses, two blocking defects each found independently by two
reviewers:
- schema.ts is a LOSSY view of the applied schema: memberships_role_check
  lives only in migration SQL (drizzle 0.30 has no check() API), so a
  regenerated baseline ships role as free text. Port it first.
- drizzle's ledger lives in the `drizzle` schema, not `public`. Dropping
  only public leaves the rows alive; the 2nd reset then no-ops and prints
  success against an empty database.
Plus: a destructive script must never read an ambient DATABASE_URL (dotenv
does not override an already-set var), and dropping legacy-peer-deps is a
resolution change INSIDE the auth stack (better-call moves to zod 4).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01K8sHMdAX2XpyuCacTHnDYv

* docs(spec): delete backfill-numbers rather than test it (owner)

Review flagged db:backfill-numbers as the one deploy step no gate covers
(backfillNumbers(db as any) compiles straight through the 0.30->0.45 API
change) and proposed running it from db:reset so it gets exercised.

Owner's call is better: the data is disposable, and Session/SortResult
repositories already assign `number` at INSERT via allocateWithRetry, so a
NULL number cannot exist on any DB built from now on. It is a one-shot
legacy heal that has been a no-op on every prod deploy since. Delete it --
the untested deploy step and its `as any` stop existing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01K8sHMdAX2XpyuCacTHnDYv

* docs(spec): cut the ceremony — one migration, final schema, minimal guard

Owner: "why are we running 17 migrations? We just need the final schema."
Correct — we ship ONE baseline generated from schema.ts. The 17 only ever
appeared in a verification diff, and that diff re-proves a fact review
already established by enumeration (memberships_role_check is the sole
object with no declarative home). Demoted to a one-time local sanity check.

Cut: the pg_dump CI gate, the journal content-hash guard (YAGNI until there
is data worth keeping), and the belt-and-braces half of the db:reset guard.
Kept: porting the CHECK into schema.ts, which is correctness, not caution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01K8sHMdAX2XpyuCacTHnDYv

* feat(deps): drizzle 0.45, drop legacy-peer-deps, squash drizzle/ to one baseline

- drizzle-orm 0.30.10 -> ^0.45.2; drizzle-kit 0.20.17 -> ^0.31.6, moved to
  devDependencies (codegen CLI; the runtime migrator imports drizzle-orm).
- .npmrc legacy-peer-deps DROPPED. Clean npm install, no ERESOLVE. This also
  fixes a latent wrong: the flag was feeding better-call zod 3 while it declares
  a zod ^4 peer. It now nests its own zod 4; app code keeps zod 3.
- drizzle.config.ts: driver:"pg" -> dialect:"postgresql"; connectionString -> url.
- db:generate: the removed generate:pg family -> config-driven `drizzle-kit generate`.
- Database type widened from `typeof db` to the shared base class PgDatabase<...>.
  PgTransaction extends PgDatabase, so a tx satisfies it and withTransaction
  typechecks — 1 file, not the 16-repository DbOrTx ripple the bead predicted.
- schema.ts: ported memberships_role_check via check() (drizzle 0.30 had no check()
  API, so it lived ONLY in migration SQL and a regenerated baseline would have
  silently shipped `role` as free text).
- schema.ts: removed the duplicate invitations_token_unique index. The column's
  .unique() already emits a constraint of that name; 0.20 hid the collision behind
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, 0.31 makes it a fatal 42P07.
- drizzle/ squashed 17 migrations -> one generated 0000_init (journal v7).
  Verified: 45/45 constraints, 32/32 indexes, identical column set, all three
  partial predicates byte-identical vs a DB built from the old 17.
- Deleted backfill-numbers (script, module, test, npm script, vercel-build step):
  Session/SortResult repos assign `number` at INSERT, so a NULL number is
  unreachable on any DB built from now on. One-shot legacy heal, now dead.
- Added scripts/db-reset.ts: drops public AND drizzle (the ledger lives there, so
  dropping public alone makes the NEXT reset no-op into an empty DB and report
  success), then re-migrates. Refuses an ambient DATABASE_URL; echo-back confirm.
- Pinned sessions_active_unique's predicate by indexdef — the squash re-runs the
  codegen path that historically ate index predicates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01K8sHMdAX2XpyuCacTHnDYv

* fix(deps): unwrap drizzle 0.45's error wrapper in every conflict detector

The DB suite caught a REAL user-visible regression: 6 failures, all
"expected 500 to be 409".

drizzle 0.45 WRAPS the driver error. What it throws is a plain Error whose
message is "Failed query: insert into sessions ...", with the real
PostgresError -- carrying `code` and `constraint_name` -- demoted to
`.cause`. All five conflict detectors read `error.code` at the TOP level, so
under 0.45 they silently return false:

  - "you already have a sort in progress" (a gentle 409) became a 500.
  - two MAX+1 allocation retries (slug, number) stopped retrying and would
    have surfaced a recoverable race as a hard failure.

src/lib/db-error-log.ts:32 already read `.code ?? .cause.code` -- the
LOGGING path knew this; the paths that ACT on the error never did. Replaced
all five copies with one shared isUniqueViolation(error, constraint) that
walks the cause chain and matches constraint_name exactly. 4 unit tests pin
the wrapped shape (no DB needed).

Also, from the architect/security re-review:
- db-reset: REFUSE A NON-TTY STDIN. The echo-back confirm was not a lock --
  `echo "host/db" | npm run db:reset` satisfied it with zero interaction,
  which is exactly what a CI job or an agent does when a prompt looks hung.
  One line; subsumes the CI/VERCEL check and the agent case. Verified.
- db-reset: GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public after recreating it -- a
  fresh `public` carries none of the original grants.
- schema: dropped the redundant sort_shares_token_unique index. The column's
  .unique() already emits a constraint; the explicit index differed only in
  NAME so BOTH existed -- two btrees per share insert for one guarantee.
  Keeping it "to match prod" is void: prod is about to be rebuilt from this
  baseline. Indexes 32 -> 31; constraints unchanged.
- Deleted the 0012_reset_elo_drafts replay test: it read that migration off
  disk to verify its one-shot data DELETEs. The squash removed the file, and
  a fresh DB has no Elo-era drafts. Its subject no longer exists.

Gates: lint 0 errors | test:ci 1304 passed | test:db 650 passed (0 failed)
| build OK | auth:verify OK. tsc's 96 errors are PRE-EXISTING -- verified
identical on main via a clean worktree; tsc is not a gate here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01K8sHMdAX2XpyuCacTHnDYv

* docs: sync ARCHITECTURE + README for the drizzle squash (/sync-docs)

ARCHITECTURE decision 33: the squash, the verified schema equivalence, the
timestamp-only migrator trap, the two facts schema.ts was hiding, drizzle
0.45's error wrapping (500-vs-409), the auth-stack zod move, and db:reset.
Flags that migration numbers 0000-0016 cited elsewhere in the doc no longer
exist as FILES (history is in git; the applied schema is unchanged).

README: db:backfill-numbers removed, db:reset documented.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01K8sHMdAX2XpyuCacTHnDYv

webServer.command: npm run build && npx next start --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3100

specs.title: authenticate
a11y: core authed screens — no serious/critical violations (light)
a11y: core authed screens — no serious/critical violations (dark)
a11y: unauthenticated login/signup — no serious/critical violations (light)
a11y: unauthenticated login/signup — no serious/critical violations (dark)
pool-first: Make items routes to the pool
both: Photo pool renders before Items, with the item preview shown
items-first: View all items routes to the items grid
empty: offers exactly one add-photos action and no pool/items sections
keyboard traversal reaches header → primary section → secondary actions → owner utilities in order
UI login redirects to /collections and the session survives middleware
after UI login, direct navigation to a protected route stays authenticated
login with bad credentials establishes no session and shows an error
login with good credentials signs in as that user
signup creates a fresh account and signs in as that user

suites.title: compare — which do you love more?

specs.title: renders the prompt, two choice cards, and quiet Tie/Skip escapes
tapping a card chooses it and the next pair (or a graceful end) appears
gentle progress text appears after a comparison is made
crash-reload: the gate drains pending decisions in queue order BEFORE the round re-renders
